nodes.label: Spike Event Recording (record=True)
nodes.rationale: Kernel lanes extract (tick, neuron) events on the GPU once per chunk into a buffer of cap events (default 262,144) and raise RecordOverflow naming the ticks rather than dropping spikes; events replace a dense full raster, which would take 152 MB per trial for 0.001 % occupancy.

nodes.label: async_eval In-Flight Work Raises Peak Memory
nodes.norm_label: async_eval in-flight work raises peak memory
nodes.rationale: Most of the fused lane's 665 MB peak is work async_eval has scheduled but not finished: a blocking eval peaks at 273 MB, and a recording lane, which waits for the previous chunk before encoding the next, keeps less work in flight.

nodes.label: Recording Overhead Is a Cost per Chunk
nodes.norm_label: recording overhead is a cost per chunk
nodes.rationale: The added time is nearly the same in every configuration (0.15 to 0.17 ms per 32-tick chunk) although hub drives fire 2.7 to 2.9x as many spikes, because stacking the spike masks, one dispatch and reading events back happen per chunk, not per spike; it weighs most where a tick is cheapest (+12.3 % on the idle sugar run).

nodes.label: Brian2 Code-Generation Target (cython 2.07 s vs numpy 8.38 s)
nodes.norm_label: brian2 code-generation target (cython 2.07 s vs numpy 8.38 s)

nodes.label: ~7x Speedup over Brian2 (0.29 s vs 2.07 s per Biological Second)
nodes.norm_label: ~7x speedup over brian2 (0.29 s vs 2.07 s per biological second)
nodes.rationale: Same model and machine, both over a full biological second. It replaces a ~213x figure published until 2026-09-15, which extrapolated Brian2 from a 200-tick run whose fixed net.run cost inflated it about thirtyfold (7.9 s per biological second at 200 ticks, 2.07 at 10,000). Against the fused lane with spike recording on, as Brian2's SpikeMonitor records, the margin is 6.2x.

nodes.label: MLX Optimisation Checklist
nodes.rationale: Ordered from cheapest to most involved: chunk with async_eval, vary the work, count bytes, fuse the chain with constants passed as arguments and contraction disabled, handle data-dependent shapes with a kernel or dense early exit, accumulate in integers, and keep a CPU float64 reference.

nodes.label: 16-Op Chain vs Fused Kernel Microbenchmark (5.9x)
nodes.rationale: 0.1333 against 0.0225 ms per step and 15.6 against 1.0 MiB moved; the chain's implied 114 GiB/s is roughly what the machine sustains, so it is bandwidth-bound, and 5.9x is a ceiling rather than the engine's gain.

nodes.label: FMA Contraction Probe (2^20 float32 Triples)
nodes.rationale: Refutes the earlier FMA explanation: over 245,246 differing elements, eager MLX and mx.compile both round a*b and + c separately, because mx.compile emits every op as its own statement and Metal's safe math mode contracts only within one expression; a hand-written kernel that writes a*b + c as one expression does contract unless the pragma turns it off.

nodes.label: #pragma clang fp contract(off)
nodes.rationale: A hand-written kernel whose reference rounds a*b and + c separately must disable contraction: without the pragma the fused lane's final v is no longer bit-identical and its spikes differ from step 6,729 on. compile_options math_mode cannot help, because safe, the strictest mode and the default, is the one that contracted.

nodes.label: Fused Elementwise Kernel (0.75 s to 0.29 s, 2.55x)
nodes.norm_label: fused elementwise kernel (0.75 s to 0.29 s, 2.55x)
nodes.rationale: A real tick also spends time on propagation that fusion does not touch, so expect a fraction of the isolated 5.9x in proportion to how much of the step is the elementwise chain.

nodes.label: print_float_constant (mlx/backend/common/compiled.h)
nodes.rationale: Uses digits10 + 1, i.e. 7 significant digits, when printing a float constant into kernel source, two short of the 9 a float32 needs to round-trip.

nodes.label: Pass Float Constants to Compiled Functions as Arguments
nodes.norm_label: pass float constants to compiled functions as arguments
nodes.rationale: Constants read from buffers instead of printed as literals make the compiled run bit-identical to the reference at 10,000 steps (same spike-count SHA-256, same final v and g); the chunked lane's compile_body=True does this and passes the parity gate, at least until the MLX fix is released.

nodes.label: Count Bytes, Not Dispatches
nodes.rationale: Splitting work into more kernels inside one eval is close to free; what costs is what each kernel reads and writes, about 2kN * itemsize per step for a chain of k ops on N elements.

nodes.label: eval() Is the Synchronisation Unit, Not the Dispatch
nodes.norm_label: eval() is the synchronisation unit, not the dispatch
nodes.rationale: One to sixteen dispatches inside one eval all cost about 0.11 ms, the round trip of submitting a command buffer and waiting for it, so mx.eval in a loop is 1.1 s of floor over 10,000 steps; this is the real reason to chunk and a much smaller effect than intermediate writes.

nodes.label: MLX Writes Every Intermediate to Memory
nodes.norm_label: mlx writes every intermediate to memory
nodes.rationale: a*b + c over N elements is two passes with a full N-element buffer between them, so a chain of 16 elementwise ops makes 16 round trips through DRAM; the chain is bandwidth-bound on intermediates nobody reads, while a fused kernel keeps the value in a register.

nodes.label: mx.compile Rounds Captured Float Constants
nodes.rationale: mx.compile prints each captured scalar constant into the generated Metal source with 7 significant digits where float32 needs 9, so two of the model's eight constants come back 1 ulp off; a strict threshold turns that into different spikes from step 120 on (48,308 against 47,499 at 10,000 steps), despite a +4 % speedup.

nodes.label: Measure Against a Tuned Baseline
nodes.rationale: The fusion win read 5.2x in an earlier version because the unfused baseline ran at a bad tuning constant, and fixing the baseline halved it; a speedup against an untuned 'before' measures your own earlier mistake.

nodes.label: Did Not Work: Believing an Unmeasured Explanation
nodes.norm_label: did not work: believing an unmeasured explanation
nodes.rationale: The fusion win was attributed to dispatch count for weeks when it was memory traffic, and mx.compile's divergence was blamed on FMA contraction when it was constant rounding; a twenty-minute microbenchmark or a few-line probe would have shown each.

nodes.label: Sparse Metal Lane Mistuned at EDGE_SPLIT 16
nodes.norm_label: sparse metal lane mistuned at edge_split 16
nodes.rationale: The old default of 16 is fastest in none of the six swept lane and drive combinations; at K=2 the sparse lane is 2.0x faster (1.5163 to 0.7491 s), so the fusion step, which had been credited against the mistuned baseline, drops from a published 5.2x to a measured 2.55x.

nodes.label: Finding 3: Intermediate Materialisation
nodes.rationale: Once propagation is sparse, the elementwise half dominates: a chain of ~16 MLX ops moves 15.6 MiB per tick through DRAM while the values fit in registers. Fusing it moves 1.0 MiB and took 0.75 s to 0.29 s, 2.55x rather than the 5.2x published against a mistuned baseline; it was first misattributed to dispatch overhead.

nodes.label: male-cns-v1.0-superclass-non-null-known-nt Materialization
nodes.rationale: Node selection and transmitter signs follow this materialization because flyBrain publishes the same one, which keeps the two engines comparable.

nodes.label: Fail-Closed Pack Compilers
nodes.rationale: Both compilers run their validation checks, 40 of them for FlyWire, and refuse to write anything if one fails.

nodes.label: 24,469,412 MaleCNS Edges Match flyBrain's Count
nodes.rationale: flyBrain publishes the same surviving edge count for the same materialization, reached through an independently written filter, which is the strongest evidence available that the selection rules are right.

nodes.label: mehrantsi/flyBrain Rust/Metal Engine (MIT)
nodes.rationale: Serves as both a performance reference and a source of ideas: its MLX lane demonstrated mx.fast.metal_kernel for CSR propagation, and its description of fusing decay/threshold work with propagation is the basis for the two-dispatch fused tick.

nodes.label: Local flyBrain Reference Build Without MuJoCo
nodes.norm_label: local flybrain reference build without mujoco
nodes.rationale: The setup script disables flyBrain's MuJoCo-dependent modules so its neural benchmark builds without MuJoCo, leaves the compute core rust/src/metal_engine.rs untouched and keeps the original lib.rs as lib.rs.orig, so comparisons run flyBrain's own engine without vendoring any of its code.

nodes.label: mx.fast.metal_kernel API
nodes.rationale: Used when only a data-dependent subset of indices carries work, which the lazy graph cannot express: the kernel is dispatched densely and its threads exit early.

nodes.label: FlyWire Benchmark Results (M4 Pro, 10,000 Ticks, Sugar Drive)
nodes.norm_label: flywire benchmark results (m4 pro, 10,000 ticks, sugar drive)
nodes.rationale: Rows marked same session were measured within minutes of each other on 2026-09-14 with pack loading and shader compilation excluded; the benchmark checks every lane against the naive baseline before reporting a time, so a lane that lost parity is marked FAIL instead of being credited with a number.

nodes.label: ~22 % Margin over flyBrain Rust/Metal
nodes.rationale: A narrow win over a small, young project that costs 7x the memory (665 vs 94 MB); flyBrain fires 16,796 spikes against 13,594 in the same run because its refractory semantics differ, so the margin at equal spike counts is smaller, and under CPU load it falls to ~10 %. Re-measured on 2026-09-15 at 22.3 %.

nodes.label: flyBrain MLX Lane (CSR metal_kernel, One Thread per Source Neuron)
nodes.norm_label: flybrain mlx lane (csr metal_kernel, one thread per source neuron)
nodes.rationale: Propagates CSR through a hand-written Metal kernel with one thread per source neuron and an early exit, the same shape as this engine's kernel; its README's remark about per-tick host synchronisation is what prompted this project.

nodes.label: Two-Dispatch Fused Tick
nodes.rationale: One Metal dispatch for propagation with atomics and one for everything else, so the elementwise work that MLX would otherwise write to memory between ops stays in registers.

nodes.label: Credit to flyBrain for metal_kernel, Fusion and Benchmark Setup
nodes.norm_label: credit to flybrain for metal_kernel, fusion and benchmark setup
nodes.rationale: Two of the three findings came from reading flyBrain: its MLX lane got to mx.fast.metal_kernel first, and kernel fusion came straight from its README (the 2.55x, second-largest step); its benchmark setup made a fair comparison possible. This engine adds the edge-split for load imbalance and a stricter parity gate.

nodes.label: Host-Bound Wall-Clock Under CPU Load
nodes.rationale: This engine rebuilds its MLX graph on the host every chunk, so CPU load slowed it by 13.9 % while flyBrain's native Rust loop moved by noise (-1.1 %); a worse local number should prompt a check of CPU load before suspecting the build.

nodes.label: Same-Session, Falsifiable Benchmarking
nodes.rationale: A benchmark nobody can falsify is not a benchmark: comparisons are measured in one session and re-measured, and figures from an earlier session that were never re-measured, such as flyBrain's MLX lanes at 3.241 and 40.62, were dropped once the Brian2 figure proved wrong for exactly that reason.

nodes.label: Chunked Steps with mx.async_eval
nodes.rationale: Queue N steps, evaluate once and let the host run ahead of the GPU; here it gained only 12 % (22.1 to 19.4 s), which showed sync was not the problem. Anything inside a chunk that reads a value back to the host collapses it, so control flow must be expressed as arithmetic.

nodes.label: Dense Dispatch with Early Exits
nodes.rationale: All 127,400 threads are dispatched every step and 127,300 return on their second instruction: the dispatch stays dense and statically sized while the memory traffic becomes sparse, which took 19.6 s to 0.75 s, the largest single step in the project. The early exit is what changed, not the scatter.

nodes.label: Did Not Work: Atomic-Counter Compaction
nodes.rationale: Two dispatches with a much smaller second grid measured 0.0572 ms against 0.0550 ms for one dense-grid kernel with early exits: the extra kernel and its dependency cost more than the smaller grid saved, and a two-instruction early exit is hard to beat.

nodes.label: Find Out What You Are Bound By
nodes.norm_label: find out what you are bound by
nodes.rationale: Host synchronisation, fixed per-step overhead and memory traffic need different fixes and guessing wrong costs days, so each gets a cheap test before any fix.

nodes.label: Lazy Graphs Cannot Express Data-Dependent Output Sizes
nodes.norm_label: lazy graphs cannot express data-dependent output sizes
nodes.rationale: 'The indices where x is true' has no size a lazy graph can know in advance, so producing it means reading a count back to the host, the synchronisation chunking exists to avoid; sparse traffic therefore needs a kernel, or a dense dispatch with early exits.

nodes.label: .at[].add() Cannot Skip Work
nodes.rationale: It touches every index it is given, so the dense baseline gathered the delayed spike mask for all 14.7 M edges and scatter-added all of them however few neurons fired, which is why runtime was flat across a 5,000x range of activity.

nodes.label: Vary the Work, Not the Step Count
nodes.norm_label: vary the work, not the step count
nodes.rationale: Varying activity 5,000x moved runtime by 2 %; flat runtime means a fixed cost per step that no tuning of the data path will help.

nodes.label: Finding 1: Dense Is the Problem, Not Synchronisation
nodes.norm_label: finding 1: dense is the problem, not synchronisation
nodes.rationale: Every tick touched all 14.7 M edges, so dense runtime was flat across a 5,000x range of activity; pure MLX cannot compact the spike list because its size is data-dependent, so mx.fast.metal_kernel with threads that exit early took 19.6 s to 0.75 s, by far the largest step.

nodes.label: Did Not Work: Two-Kernel Spike Compaction
nodes.norm_label: did not work: two-kernel spike compaction
nodes.rationale: Compacting the firing neurons into a list with an atomic counter and dispatching over MAXS*K instead of N*K threads was slower, 0.0572 against 0.0550 ms: the second dispatch costs more than the smaller grid saves.

nodes.rationale: On MaleCNS names need no dict: the compiler writes the annotation table's type, instance, class and flywireType next to the pack, and a name selects every neuron whose instance it is or, failing that, whose type it is ('MN9_R' is one neuron, 'MN9' both). nodes.rationale: The proboscis motor neuron that the published example notebook reads out, reused as the readout of the wiring control, the notebook gate and the activity film.

nodes.label: Published-Notebook Validation Gate
nodes.rationale: Runs upstream's example notebook with its code cells unchanged and model resolving to lif.experiment, then compares its five experiments with upstream's Brian2 files at seeds 0 and 1000. Brian2's random input is not this engine's, so agreement can only be in distribution: each neuron's rate is compared as a z score, and the two seeds are compared with each other to show how far two runs of the same model fall. The gate caught that upstream's sugarR file was written at 200 Hz while default_params now says 150 Hz.

nodes.label: run_exp: Upstream-Compatible Experiment API
nodes.rationale: Keeps upstream's signature, default_params and parquet output so a researcher's existing notebook runs with its code cells unchanged, judged worth more than a tidier native rate-first API. Only t_run, n_run, r_poi and r_poi2 can change because the model constants are compiled in, and trial n draws its input with seed + n. 30 one-second trials take 10.05 s against about 77 s extrapolated for Brian2, which rebuilds the network for every trial.

nodes.label: Degree-Preserving Shuffled-Wiring Control
nodes.rationale: Every neuron keeps its in- and out-degree and the signs and sizes of its outgoing synapses while each connection goes to a random target. With the same input spikes MN9 fires at 67.30 Hz on the FlyWire wiring and not at all on shuffles with seeds 0 to 4 (96 against 408 neurons firing at all), so it is the wiring, not the degrees or the signs, that carries the sugar signal to MN9.

nodes.label: Sugar-GRN Drive (21 Right Sugar-Sensing GRNs)
nodes.rationale: Poisson input at 100 Hz as in the published notebook, or 150 Hz in the benchmark. A sparse drive on FlyWire (1.36 spikes and 209 outgoing edges per tick), so edge_split 1 suits the fused lane and 2 the sparse Metal lane.

nodes.label: Control Demo Figure (MN9, Real vs Shuffled Wiring)
nodes.norm_label: control demo figure (mn9, real vs shuffled wiring)
nodes.rationale: Two rows of rate-over-time bar charts, real wiring left and degree-matched shuffle right: the top row asks whether the wiring carries the sugar signal to MN9, the bottom row shows the identical input reaching both packs. Each row shares one y axis so its panels compare directly, and the empty shuffled panel carries a note so silence is not read as a missing plot.

nodes.label: Degree-Preserving Shuffle Control
nodes.rationale: Randomises which neuron reaches which while every neuron keeps its in- and out-degree (and each source its signs and total output), so degree statistics cannot explain a response that disappears on the shuffle; seed 0 is the shuffle shown.

nodes.label: Wiring, Not Degrees, Carries the Sugar Signal to MN9
nodes.norm_label: wiring, not degrees, carries the sugar signal to mn9
nodes.rationale: With the same input on both packs, MN9 fires at 67.3 Hz on the FlyWire v630 wiring and not once in 30 trials on the degree-matched shuffle, and brain activity falls from 290,963 spikes in 408 neurons to 75,091 spikes in 96. Degrees are held fixed, so the specific wiring is what routes the sugar signal to MN9.

nodes.label: Propagation Cost per K (2, 21 and 107 Active Rows)
nodes.norm_label: propagation cost per k (2, 21 and 107 active rows)
nodes.rationale: Per propagation the best K is 2 when the work is tiny and 8 to 16 when it is not (K=1 at 107 active rows takes 2.5x as long as K=8); the small-load rows are flat because they are eval floor, not work.

nodes.label: Tunable Unroll K for Skewed CSR Rows
nodes.norm_label: tunable unroll k for skewed csr rows
nodes.rationale: One thread per row collapses on skewed rows (out-degree 0 to 9,615, mean 115, and the touched rows are the longest), so K threads share a row and stride through it. There is no single best K and the engine cannot choose it at runtime without a host readback, so it stays a caller-set parameter: an honest limitation rather than a missing feature.

nodes.label: edge_split Knob (Threads per Neuron Edge List)
nodes.norm_label: edge_split knob (threads per neuron edge list)
nodes.rationale: Every neuron gets that many threads every tick and nearly all exit at once because their neuron did not fire, so a larger value helps only when the neurons that fire carry long edge lists; the best value follows the drive and, on a sparse drive, the lane.

nodes.label: edge_split End-to-End Sweep (K=1 to 16)
nodes.rationale: Measured per pack, drive and lane as a median of 7 interleaved runs: the other drive's value costs 2.23x to 2.52x in the fused lane and 1.31x to 1.45x in the sparse Metal lane, and 16 is fastest in no row.

nodes.label: Finding 2: Out-Degree Load Imbalance
nodes.rationale: Out-degree runs from 0 to 9,615 with a mean of 115 and the driven neurons are the biggest hubs, so one thread per neuron serialises about 9,600 atomics while 127,399 threads idle.

nodes.label: No Host Readback of Spike Counts
nodes.norm_label: no host readback of spike counts
nodes.rationale: The engine cannot pick edge_split at runtime without reading the spike count back to the host, which is exactly the synchronisation the design avoids, so the value stays a caller-set parameter.

nodes.label: atomic_outputs=True Makes Every Output Atomic
nodes.rationale: There is no per-output setting, so a kernel with one atomic accumulator and ordinary outputs must write the ordinary ones with atomic_store_explicit, and the compile error does not point at the cause.

nodes.label: Cache Kernel Objects and Template Their Source
nodes.norm_label: cache kernel objects and template their source
nodes.rationale: Building the kernel object per call recompiles it, so cache it in a dict keyed on whatever is templated into the source; string templating one variant per unroll factor lets a constant be a compile-time literal.

nodes.label: mx.fast.metal_kernel Traps
nodes.rationale: The traps in the order they were hit: source is a body with no signature, grid counts threads rather than threadgroups as CUDA does, and scalars must be passed as mx.array([float(x)]) since an np.float32 raises.

nodes.label: Cross-Lane Parity Gate (Spike-Count SHA-256)
nodes.rationale: Speed claims are worthless without a correctness gate: all four lanes must give identical per-neuron spike counts, compared by SHA-256 over the full vector, and bitwise final v and g. It also holds with a silencing mask, where it compares two unrelated mechanisms, and with recording, where the naive lane's host np.nonzero checks the kernel lanes' GPU event extraction.

nodes.label: Integer Atomics Are Deterministic, Float Atomics Are Not
nodes.norm_label: integer atomics are deterministic, float atomics are not
nodes.rationale: Float addition is not associative, so float atomic_fetch_add depends on thread completion order and differs between runs and machines; int32 atomic_fetch_add_explicit is bit-reproducible, so an accumulation with fixed-point structure, here synaptic contact counts scaled once afterwards, buys reproducibility for free.

nodes.label: Sort an Atomically Compacted Set on the Host
nodes.norm_label: sort an atomically compacted set on the host
nodes.rationale: With an atomic counter the slot order is non-deterministic but the set written is not, so sorting on the host makes the result reproducible again.

nodes.label: int32 Contact-Count Accumulation
nodes.rationale: Synaptic arrivals accumulate as int32 contact counts and the 0.275 mV factor is applied afterwards; integer addition is associative and cannot overflow here, so the result does not depend on thread completion order, unlike float atomics.

nodes.label: Brian2 (unless refractory) Write Shielding
nodes.rationale: Shields the variable from every write, synaptic input included: a spike arriving at a refractory neuron leaves g at exactly zero before and after the refractory period, dropped rather than queued.

nodes.label: Brian2 Spike-Time Gate (800-Neuron Subnetwork)
nodes.rationale: A connected 800-neuron subnetwork driven by a fixed spike train keeps RNG differences out of the comparison, so the float64 oracle must match Brian2 spike for spike, and the command fails if the fused lane leaves out or adds more than 5 % of Brian2's spikes.

nodes.label: Source-Major CSR Pack Format
nodes.rationale: Both compilers write this one format, so every engine lane runs either connectome unchanged.

nodes.label: Brian2-Preserving Tick Ordering
nodes.rationale: Each tick keeps Brian2's order: closed-form update of v and g for non-refractory neurons, strict v > -45 mV threshold, propagation delayed by 1.8 ms through source-major CSR, signed synaptic counts and external input, then reset, refractory update and delay-ring store.

nodes.label: Closed-Form Update Coefficients from Brian2 method='linear'
nodes.norm_label: closed-form update coefficients from brian2 method='linear'
nodes.rationale: The update coefficients in core.py are transcribed from the code Brian2 generates for method='linear', so the closed-form update stays bit-identical to Brian2's.

nodes.label: Keep a CPU float64 Reference
nodes.rationale: Metal has no float64 at all, so telling 'my semantics are wrong' from 'float32 rounded differently' needs a CPU float64 reference; the NumPy oracle proved a one-event difference was rounding and not a bug.

nodes.label: float32 Rounding at the Strict Threshold
nodes.norm_label: float32 rounding at the strict threshold
nodes.rationale: The float32 lanes match Brian2's counts in three of four configurations but move spikes by a tick after 18 to 35 ms, mostly earlier; all four MLX lanes record identical events, so this is rounding at the strict threshold, unavoidable without float64 on the GPU.

nodes.label: Metal Has No float64
nodes.rationale: Without float64 on the GPU, a CPU float64 oracle is the only way to tell wrong semantics apart from float32 rounding.

nodes.label: Open Discrepancy: Conductance During Refractoriness
nodes.rationale: flyBrain's README says incoming conductance can accumulate during refractoriness, while Brian2 2.10.1 drops those writes. On the same sugar drive this engine fires 13,594 spikes as shipped and 16,382 with that gate removed, against flyBrain's 16,796, closing 87 % of the gap; the remaining 414 are unexplained, and earlier published figures (13,354, 17,315, 819) matched no recorded run and were superseded.

nodes.label: Did Not Work: Trusting StateMonitor Timestamps
nodes.norm_label: did not work: trusting statemonitor timestamps
nodes.rationale: Brian2 records with when='start', so monitor row t holds the state at the end of tick t-1; read as same-tick state it fakes a one-tick lag, which prompted two wrong fixes to the refractory and delay constants. The correct values are the plain quotients, 22 and 18 ticks.

nodes.norm_label: lb3b and lb3c sweet-sensing taste neurons (gr64f-gal4)

nodes.rationale: A male specimen covering brain and ventral nerve cord, from a different laboratory than FlyWire, so results from the two packs are not comparable.

nodes.label: Accumulating Scatter Is .at[].add() (scatter_add)
nodes.rationale: arr[idx] = vals with repeated indices is last-write-wins and silently wrong; arr.at[idx].add(vals) lowers to scatter_add with GPU atomic adds and is the intended path at any size, since MLX 0.32.2 has no bincount, segment_sum, index_add, public scatter_add or mx.scatter. The section was headed 'There is no accumulating scatter' until a reply on the MLX discussion corrected it.

nodes.label: Equal-Work Scatter Benchmark (1.1610 vs 1.1463 ms)
nodes.rationale: Scattering all 14.7 M edges took 1.1610 ms with .at[].add() and 1.1463 ms with a hand-written kernel doing one integer atomic per edge (median of 15 evals of 8 scatters, identical sums), and the scatter is only about half of dense propagation (2.1404 ms with the gather and where); the kernel wins by running atomics only along the rows that fired.

nodes.label: .at[].add() on a Fixed Index Set
nodes.rationale: When the index set is fixed, .at[].add() on the ~100 driven indices replaced scattering through a full zeros(N) buffer and a mask, which had cost 20 % of the step.

nodes.label: Self-Sustaining Abdominal VNC State (A7 to A10)
nodes.norm_label: self-sustaining abdominal vnc state (a7 to a10)
nodes.rationale: The film's rise lives in the abdominal neuromeres (69 of the 85 neurons above 100 Hz, 55 of them in A7 to A10), and silencing the outgoing synapses of all 2,156 abdominal VNC neurons keeps the VNC share at 25.1 to 29.9 %. Once reached, a trial holds the state without input, but not every trial reaches it, so trials are counted one by one: a pooled mean over trials that settled differently describes none of them.

nodes.label: MaleCNS Sweet-Taste Activity Film
nodes.rationale: A visualization, not evidence: spike times come from the model and positions from the annotation table, while projection, colours, haze and slow motion are drawing choices, and the constants were fitted to FlyWire, not this connectome. demo.sh redraws it with the same bytes (sha256 beb947e2) so the checked-in figure can be re-derived rather than trusted.

nodes.label: Apple Silicon and Metal Only
nodes.rationale: Portability is deliberately out of scope: the engine depends on Metal, and that is the point of the repository.

nodes.label: Two Connectome Packs: FlyWire v630 vs MaleCNS v1.0
nodes.norm_label: two connectome packs: flywire v630 vs malecns v1.0
nodes.rationale: Different animals from different laboratories (a female brain only against a male brain and ventral nerve cord with 708 VNC and 107 brain leg and wing motor neurons), so spike counts are not comparable across the packs.

nodes.label: TuragaLab/flybody
nodes.rationale: Cited to mark scope: an embodied fly with learned control is a different project with a different goal.

nodes.label: LgLG1a_R Taste Neurons of the VNC
nodes.norm_label: lglg1a_r taste neurons of the vnc

nodes.label: MaleCNS Benchmark (2,000 Ticks, 100 Hubs, K=8)
nodes.rationale: Re-measured on 2026-09-15 within 0.5 % with every lane still passing parity, and kept rather than replaced because the original rows are one coherent set.

nodes.label: Stimulus Survey (Film Stimulus and Seven Others)
nodes.norm_label: stimulus survey (film stimulus and seven others)
nodes.rationale: Runs the film's stimulus and seven others at 100 Hz for 30 trials each and counts the spikes in every 100 ms by region, showing that the film's rising VNC share (28.6 to 66.9 %) is a property of this model on this connectome that not every stimulus brings out.

nodes.label: Making MLX Fast: Notes from One Real Workload
nodes.norm_label: making mlx fast: notes from one real workload
nodes.rationale: The workload is a neural simulation but nothing depends on that: the diagnostics apply to any loop that steps a few large arrays many times. The model went from 22.0 s to 0.29 s per simulated second, and none of it came from removing host synchronisation, which is where the search started.

nodes.label: drosophila-brain-mlx
nodes.rationale: Reimplements the published Shiu et al. LIF model with the same parameters and tick ordering so that one second of brain time costs about a third of a second of wall clock instead of two; nothing is trained or learned, and the engine integrates membrane voltage through the fixed, electron-microscope-traced FlyWire wiring.

nodes.label: Shiu et al. Whole-Brain Drosophila LIF Model (bioRxiv 2023)
nodes.norm_label: shiu et al. whole-brain drosophila lif model (biorxiv 2023)

nodes.label: Tastekin et al. Drosophila Taste-Feeding Connectome (bioRxiv 2025)
nodes.norm_label: tastekin et al. drosophila taste-feeding connectome (biorxiv 2025)

nodes.label: Shiu Constants Fitted to FlyWire, Not MaleCNS
nodes.norm_label: shiu constants fitted to flywire, not malecns
nodes.rationale: The model constants were fitted to the FlyWire brain and not refitted to MaleCNS, which adds the ventral nerve cord; compile_pack_malecns records this in the pack manifest so MaleCNS runs carry the caveat.

nodes.label: Implementation-Only Contribution
nodes.rationale: The project reimplements a published model and contributes an implementation only: the model, its parameters, the connectivity data and the science behind them belong to Shiu et al. and the connectome projects.

nodes.label: No Upstream Data or Code Redistributed
nodes.norm_label: no upstream data or code redistributed
nodes.rationale: Upstream files, the MaleCNS tables and flyBrain are downloaded or built locally by scripts rather than shipped, which keeps the repository an implementation only and leaves each source under its own distribution terms.

nodes.label: No Per-Tick Output Port for a Body
nodes.norm_label: no per-tick output port for a body
nodes.rationale: Upstream computes rates from spike counts only, which spike_counts already covers; coupling to flybody, FlyGym or flyBrain's MuJoCo scene would need a per-tick port and a realtime brake and still would not own the gait generators, odour decoders and landing gates between motor neurons and joints, so it waits for a partner body.

nodes.label: Palette-Indexed Animated PNG (100 Frames, 80 ms Each, 251 Colours)
nodes.norm_label: palette-indexed animated png (100 frames, 80 ms each, 251 colours)
nodes.rationale: One frame per 10 ms bin of a 1 s run gives 100 frames of 480x674 pixels, each shown for 80 ms (eight times slower than biological time) and looping; a 251-colour palette (31 fog levels times 8 activity levels, plus text, track and bar colours) keeps each pixel to one byte, and every scanline is Paeth-filtered and deflated, so the frames are stored losslessly without an imaging library.

nodes.label: Orthographic View Turning Once About the CNS Long Axis
nodes.norm_label: orthographic view turning once about the cns long axis
nodes.rationale: The camera turns once about the CNS's long axis over the 100 frames (close to a side view at 250 ms, close to the mirror image of the first frame at 500 ms, nearly back at the start at 1000 ms), so the depth of the 3D soma cloud reads from motion; the view is fitted so every position stays in the picture at every angle.

nodes.label: Blue Soma-Position Fog (Brain Above, Ventral Nerve Cord Below)
nodes.norm_label: blue soma-position fog (brain above, ventral nerve cord below)
nodes.rationale: Every neuron that has a soma position in the MaleCNS annotation table is splatted at its projected position, blurred, drawn denser where nearer and gamma-lifted so the thin ventral nerve cord's outline shows; the haze gives the spikes an anatomical frame (the brain with both optic lobes at the top, the ventral nerve cord below) without drawing individual cells.

nodes.label: Orange-to-White Spike Glow per 10 ms Bin
nodes.norm_label: orange-to-white spike glow per 10 ms bin
nodes.rationale: A neuron is lit at its soma position by how often it spiked in the current 10 ms bin, summed over the run's 30 trials: orange for a low rate through yellow to near-white for a high one, with a blurred glow so a single neuron reads as a dot against the fog. Neurons without a soma position, the driven LB3b and LB3c neurons among them, spike but are not drawn.

nodes.label: Time Label and Progress Bar (10 ms to 1000 ms)
nodes.norm_label: time label and progress bar (10 ms to 1000 ms)
nodes.rationale: Below the scene a 5x7 bitmap-font label gives the end of the current 10 ms bin and an orange bar fills a grey track, placing each frame within the one-second trial.

nodes.label: Activity Film: MaleCNS Spikes at Soma Positions (Animated PNG)
nodes.norm_label: activity film: malecns spikes at soma positions (animated png)

nodes.label: Independent Pack Audit Through a Different Code Path
nodes.norm_label: independent pack audit through a different code path
nodes.rationale: verify_pack audits a written pack afterwards through a different code path so a bug cannot confirm itself, re-deriving the MaleCNS node selection and transmitter signs from the raw tables rather than importing them.

nodes.label: Spiking Gathers at the Posterior Tip of the Ventral Nerve Cord
nodes.norm_label: spiking gathers at the posterior tip of the ventral nerve cord
nodes.rationale: What the film shows: at 10 ms only a handful of central-brain neurons and a few ventral nerve cord neurons are lit; by 250 ms spiking spreads through the central brain and gathers at the posterior tip of the VNC, where the abdominal neuromeres lie; at 500 and 1000 ms the VNC has more than twice as many lit pixels as the brain, about two thirds of them at that tip, while brain spiking stays scattered through the central brain and the optic lobes stay almost unlit. The film locates activity without explaining it: a visualization, not evidence.

nodes.label: decay_v and v0_term Constants (1 ulp Off When Printed)
nodes.norm_label: decay_v and v0_term constants (1 ulp off when printed)

nodes.label: Silencing Mask (silenced=)
nodes.rationale: Sets every synapse from a neuron to zero weight, which is what the published model's code does although its README says 'to and from'; the code produced the published results, so this follows the code. A silenced neuron still integrates, spikes, counts and may be driven; kernel lanes empty its edge range and dense lanes zero its edge counts, at -1.16 % to +0.01 % cost.

nodes.label: Keep the Exit to the One Read That Decides It
nodes.norm_label: keep the exit to the one read that decides it
nodes.rationale: Whatever is tested before return is paid by all N*K threads: a second per-row flag in the exit cost +0.9 % at K=1 up to +73 % at K=8 on an isolated kernel, and +29 % or +66 % of the engine step at K=8 depending on the stimulus; moving the flag into an end-of-row array read only after the exit cost at most +2.5 %.

nodes.label: Model Constants Fixed at Compile Time
nodes.norm_label: model constants fixed at compile time
nodes.rationale: v_th, tau and the other constants are compiled in so the closed-form coefficients stay bit-identical to Brian2's; per-run constant sweeps are possible but nobody has asked.

nodes.label: Did Not Work: Testing the Silencing Mask in the Early Exit
nodes.norm_label: did not work: testing the silencing mask in the early exit
nodes.rationale: One extra read, but all N*K threads run it, including those that exit: +36 % of the fused tick on MaleCNS at edge_split 8, +74.5 % at 16, nothing at 1. Silencing now empties the neuron's edge range, which only threads whose neuron spiked read.
